text: Radiation transport and moment methods Radiation transport resolves intensity in space, direction and frequency. Moment methods reduce the angular dimension but require closure for information removed by integration. Problem and representative equations Use frequency-integrated grey intensity I in a static medium, with isotropic emissivity η and absorption coefficient κ of inverse-length units; omit scattering here. Define E=(1/c)∫I dΩ, F=∫nI dΩ and P=(1/c)∫nnI dΩ. Moment equations for E and F require a prescription for P. 1c∂tI+n⋅∇I=η−κI,∂tE+∇⋅F=4πη−cκE,c−2∂tF+∇⋅P=−κF/c.c1​∂t​I+n⋅∇I=η−κI,∂t​E+∇⋅F=4πη−cκE,c−2∂t​F+∇⋅P=−κF/c. Algorithm Discrete ordinates discretizes angle directly; moment methods close P=D E. M1 obtains D locally from E and F, while flux-limited diffusion instead approximates F from the gradient of E. Check optically thick and free-streaming limits and couple matter exchange through a consistent energy balance. Conditions and pitfalls M1 generally cannot propagate crossing beams independently. FLD ties flux to the energy gradient, limiting shadows and strongly anisotropic fields. A reduced light speed changes transport/relaxation scales and must be justified against the physical time scales of interest. The companion retains a one-dimensional steady purely absorbing slab with specified inflow, solving μ∂xI=−κI. General radiation moment closures, scattering, time dependence, multiple frequencies and fluid coupling are unvalidated. What to check Test exponential absorption, isotropic diffusion, free streaming/shadows and crossing beams separately. Check E≥0, |F|≤cE, matter-plus-radiation energy and angular/spatial/time convergence. Distinguish closure error from discretization error. Use directional Beer–Lambert solutions and a continuum-angle exponential integral, separating upwind spatial error at fixed ordinates from angular-quadrature error with exact ray propagation. Check inflow–outflow versus volume absorption and positivity separately; a balance check alone does not establish angular-distribution accuracy. At optical depths 0.1/0.7/3, cross-check the continuum-angle reference using expn and a separate adaptive QUADPACK quadrature. Independent transport sampling draws μ=√U for the incident flux and counts transmission as a Bernoulli variable. Check binomial intervals and RMSE over 64 finite-sample replicates; nominal 95% coverage is not claimed for arbitrary inputs or samples. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Discrete-ordinate radiation transport through an absorbing slab Computation for a fixed target Discretize steady pure-absorption transfer in angle and space, checking Beer–Lambert rays and integrated exit flux. Multiple scattering, thermal emission, frequency redistribution, moving media and radiation–fluid coupling are unimplemented. This does not reproduce full DISORT functionality/stabilization.
